text: Is there any influenza data in the E. coli records here?

Abstract
This analysis tested whether any records associated with Escherichia coli in the indexed ecosystem also carry influenza-related infectious-agent annotations. We queried the NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) for E. coli across two record types: Dataset and Sample. We then faceted those matches by infectiousAgent.name to identify whether “influenza” or any influenza virus appears among the infectious agents recorded for these E. coli entries. The Dataset facet returned 1 matching record, with infectiousAgent.name equal to “escherichia coli” and no influenza terms. The Sample facet returned 0 matching records, so no infectious-agent facets were present. Quantitatively, influenza-associated entries among E. coli datasets were 0 of 1 (0%); among E. coli samples the count was 0 because no samples matched the species filter. This matters for data reuse and cross-pathogen analyses: it indicates that the current E. coli records in this index do not include influenza annotations in their infectious agent field, reducing the likelihood of co-annotated influenza content or mixed-pathogen data under E. coli in this resource.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli is a bacterial species widely studied in microbiology. Influenza viruses (e.g., Influenza A) are RNA viruses of public health importance. Determining whether influenza-related data exists within E. coli records helps assess cross-pathogen annotations, potential co-infection datasets, and data curation consistency.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether any influenza infectious-agent annotations were present within records filtered by the E. coli species in this data ecosystem.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Assess whether influenza-related infectious-agent data appears in records associated with E. coli. Hypothesis: No influenza infectious-agent annotations are present among E. coli records.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We used facet counts on the infectiousAgent.name field within records filtered to species.name:"Escherichia coli". We examined both Dataset and Sample record types to capture curated datasets and sample-level records.
Materials.
- NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE), accessed via nde_facet_counts (functions.nde_facet_counts).
Procedures.
- Call 1: nde_facet_counts with fields="infectiousAgent.name", query='species.name:"Escherichia coli"', record_type="Dataset", top_n=50.
- Call 2: nde_facet_counts with fields="infectiousAgent.name", query='species.name:"Escherichia coli"', record_type="Sample", top_n=50.
Statistical Analysis.
- We read counts from facets.infectiousAgent.name.values[].count and total_with_field. For Dataset records, influenza presence was defined as any facet value containing influenza; none were returned. Proportion of influenza among E. coli datasets: 0/1 = 0%. For Sample records, matching_records=0 and total_with_field=0, so proportions are not applicable.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Infectious agent facets among E. coli Dataset records.

| record_type | matching_records | infectiousAgent.name value | count | total_with_field | influenza_present |
|-------------|------------------|----------------------------|-------|------------------|-------------------|
| Dataset     | 1                | escherichia coli           | 1     | 1                | 0                 |

Table 2. Infectious agent facets among E. coli Sample records.

| record_type | matching_records | total_with_field | facet_values_present |
|-------------|------------------|------------------|----------------------|
| Sample      | 0                | 0                | No                   |

Findings.
- Dataset records: 1 E. coli dataset matched; infectiousAgent.name facet contained “escherichia coli” only (count=1). Influenza count=0; proportion 0/1=0%.
- Sample records: 0 E. coli samples matched; no facets returned.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. Within records filtered to species.name:"Escherichia coli", no influenza infectious-agent annotations were present; the single Dataset record was annotated with escherichia coli only. The Sample index had no E. coli matches to facet on.
Context. The facet results show only “escherichia coli” for the infectious agent among E. coli datasets [1], and no Sample records were present to inspect [2].
Limitations. The analysis reflects the current NDE index and its annotations. Faceting relies on recorded infectiousAgent.name; if influenza-related content exists but is not annotated in this field, it will not appear. The small number of E. coli Dataset records (n=1) limits generalizability. Sample records returned zero matches, so no infectious-agent information could be assessed there. Results are restricted to this ecosystem’s sources and curation.
Conclusion & Future Directions. No influenza infectious-agent annotations were found among E. coli records in this index. Future queries could:
- Broaden to all records where infectiousAgent.name contains “Influenza” to assess overall influenza coverage in the ecosystem.
- Search for co-mention of “Escherichia coli” in titles/descriptions without the species filter to detect possible mixed-pathogen studies.
- Examine repository-level records (e.g., ENA/SRA) for E. coli datasets with influenza in free text fields.

References
[1] NIAID Data Ecosystem – facet counts (Dataset): https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=50
[2] NIAID Data Ecosystem – facet counts (Sample): https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Sample%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=50

Acknowledgments
We thank the NIAID Data Ecosystem for indexed records and facet-count services.
